question: Are C6 (Isaac/DROID) and C8 (WidowX/Bridge) grasp rates comparable, or confounded by different outcome-label definitions?
verdict: DEFINITIONS_CLOSE_BUT_NOT_IDENTICAL_IN_EFFECT — shared scorer and C6-rule match; C8-comparable cell uses transport_incomplete only because C8 has zero wrong_goal_region.

agent_a_audit_correction.action: Report both C6-rule and transport_incomplete-only rates at 128 and 384 milestones; track wrong_goal_region_share per scenario as n grows

code_references.c8_composition: c8_confirmatory_composition_by_scenario_*.json (grasp_achieved = episodes - no_grasp; transport_incomplete counts as grasp)
code_references.shared_scorer: experiments/online_correction_v4/droid_scorer.py build_terminal_scorer → HorizontalDroidTerminalScorer for both containment and second_stack fixtures

natural_grasp_detector.note: Natural-grasp trigger eligibility is separate from operational grasp rate; both families use NaturalGraspDetector in runner.py

magnitude_gap_interpretation: C6 'grasp' episodes at n≈63 are predominantly transport_incomplete (partial carry before timeout), not success or wrong_goal_region. Same label on C8 yields lower rates — likely platform physics/policy behavior, not definitional confound. Cross-platform contrast (platform_scenario_grasp_contrast.csv) remains not estimable until both families reach registered coverage.
registered_estimand: platform_x_scenario_grasp_interaction with Holm handling; currently insufficient_coverage_not_estimable
action_if_divergence_found: Would require harmonizing reporters or re-deriving from accepted ledgers only — not needed; definitions already match.
